niche: a nonprofit hospice organisation's eight Medicare hospice provider numbers: the FY2026 aggregate cap repayment each accrues at the December 2026 close, each beneficiary counted under the proportional method on the hospice days they will receive in every hospice and year, stays still open and returns after a live discharge included
analyst_test: With every file read and the proportional method applied, the easy route reads each FY2026 beneficiary's share on the hospice days recorded through the close, or runs each stay still open to its expected end and treats a beneficiary discharged alive as finished, and accrues a repayment at too few of the eight provider numbers, missing the one whose FY2026 cohort holds the most live discharges.
domain_test: The cap liability under the proportional method is hospice finance's own estimate: a beneficiary counts as their FY2026 days at the hospice over the hospice days they receive in every hospice and year, so the field projects the days still to come from each beneficiary's state at the close (a stay still open and how long it has run, a live discharge and how long ago); no other field shares out a capped amount on its members' lifetime days.
layer2_pattern: own:a capped credit shared on each member's lifetime days, projected from the member's state at the close (an open stay by its length so far, a live discharge by its time out)

spine.entity: one hospice election at one provider number

driver: A unit's credit for a period is each member's share of the member's lifetime total, and the total counts every later spell, including spells after a member leaves and comes back; reading each share on the total recorded to date, or running only the open spells to their end, overstates the credit for every member still accruing and every member who left but will return, so the total is the recorded part plus the expected remainder for the member's state, read from the history of members in the same state.
driver_concrete: Each FY2026 beneficiary counts under the hospice cap as their FY2026 days at the provider number over the hospice days they will receive in every hospice and year; at the December close a stay still open is expected to run longer the longer it has already run, and a beneficiary discharged alive often re-elects hospice later, so each share is read on the days to date plus the days expected from the beneficiary's state, taken from the organisation's own elections since 2016.
stump: The default path reads each beneficiary's share on the hospice days recorded through the close, or runs each open stay to its average end and treats every live discharge as finished, and accrues a repayment at too few provider numbers, because it never asks whether a beneficiary discharged alive is done or how much longer a long stay will run.

differentiation.task157: task157 forecasts how many of a lapsed group return inside a window from the calendar earlier waves kept; here each member's returns enter that member's lifetime total of days, which divides a capped credit, and the expected remainder is read per member from the member's own state at the close (a stay open so many days, a live discharge so many days ago), with no wave calendar.
differentiation.task192: task192 v2 counts the units of a cohort that will show an event before a terminal end, with the terminal end as a competing exit; here no event is counted: each member's lifetime days are projected to divide a share, and the members who left alive are the ones still accruing days.
differentiation.task201: task201 recovers the unrecorded opening interval of each event from a parallel instrumented channel; here every day already given is recorded, and the unrecorded part is the tail of each member's days after the close, projected from the history of members in the same state.
differentiation.task445: task445 completes a still-open period's total for reporters not yet in; here every FY2026 day is recorded and nothing is completed, and what the share needs is each member's days in later years, which enter its denominator.
